topic: Grover's Algorithm: Quantum Speedup for Search
target_audience: Undergraduate students with basic knowledge of quantum mechanics (superposition, entanglement, qubits) and linear algebra.

sections.title: The Problem: Searching an Unsorted Database
lecture_lines: Classical search is slow in large unsorted lists.
We check items one by one, which is inefficient.
Worst case requires checking every single item.

sections.title: Classical vs. Quantum Search - A Glimpse of Hope
lecture_lines: Quantum computers offer a search speedup.
Find items in sqrt(N) steps, not N.

sections.title: Key Ingredients: Superposition and Amplitude Amplification
lecture_lines: These are key to quantum search speed.

sections.title: The Grover Iteration: Amplifying the Target
lecture_lines: The Grover iteration has two parts.
Oracle marks the item; diffusion amplifies it.
This process repeats to boost the target.

sections.title: How Many Iterations? The Sweet Spot
lecture_lines: Too few or too many iterations harm results.
Find the sweet spot for maximum speedup.

sections.title: Applications and Future
lecture_lines: It’s a key step in quantum computing.
